papers.title: Quarryman's note
lines: The Penrhyn men were out for three years. The children went hungry, and they did not give in.
Whatever else, we held on. Tell them it was not for nothing.

papers.title: Eisteddfod entry slip
lines: Choir: eight tenors, nine sopranos, one man who is merely moving his lips.
Piece: 'Calon Lan', by arrangement, with feeling. Expected result: tears and a medal.

trail.clue: The choir's old prize cup is hidden near the big rock. The chairman says it is 'in a safe place'.

papers.title: Ferry ticket, 1963
lines: Holyhead to Dun Laoghaire, single. A child's ticket, and a note on the back:
'Going to see Nain in Dublin. Mam says be good. I am.'

papers.title: Hafod note
lines: We drive the sheep up for summer, and live in the hut, and sing to keep the weather off.
Come at Michaelmas and bring bread. The dog will eat it unless you mention hunger first.

papers.title: Postcard from Llanfair
lines: I am writing from the village with the longest railway-station name in Europe.
It took four postcards to write the address. I have run out of stamps and breath.

papers.title: Welsh lesson note
lines: Bore da is good morning. Nos da is good night. Diolch is thank you, and you will need it often.
Practice on the nearest sheep, who will not correct you.

trail.clue: A language teacher left a tin of tea-money near the hedge, 'for the next learner'.
